clues.kinetics: A high-fat meal raises peak exposure 5-fold and AUC 4-fold. It is more than 94% protein bound and is excreted mainly in feces.
clues.substance: A crystalline solid of molecular weight 314.46 that is insoluble in water; no salt form is named.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as a 100 mg/mL oral solution, dosed twice daily.
clues.safety: No boxed warning. Contraindicated in hypersensitivity to the drug or its ingredients; diarrhea and transaminase elevations are among the most common reactions.
clues.indication: Seizures associated with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, Dravet syndrome or tuberous sclerosis complex, in patients aged 1 year and older.
clues.mechanism: Its anticonvulsant mechanism is unknown, and it does not appear to act through the classic receptors of its chemical family.
